answer: An agent economy can require one radio beacon per identity, sealed at a unique surveyed vertex for 90 days. Three towers issue simultaneous random challenges; each beacon must reply within the light-speed window for its vertex, timed from a wharf tower, a zenith tower, and a third tower. Auditors compare round-trip times in sealed logs: replies for a second vertex from the same beacon arrive too late or match its timing, triggering removal. An honest agent installs one beacon once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 beacons at 1,000 distinct sites, since one device cannot occupy two vertices at once.
